facts.fact: La Nation reports that the National Assembly adopted unanimously, on 30 June 2025, the Digital Code of nearly 800 articles, which covers regulating online commerce among other areas; the article does not say it has been promulgated or is in force.

TechAfrica News reports that Djibouti's first Digital Code, eight books and nearly 800 articles including Book IV E-Commerce and Book V Consumer Rights, was passed by the National Assembly and announced by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation; the headline says enacted but the text gives no promulgation or entry-into-force date.

facts.fact: Jones Day reports that on 30 June 2025 the National Assembly passed the Digital Code (eight volumes, nearly 800 articles, covering e-commerce, cryptology service providers, data protection and cybersecurity), and that the law was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel, and to be supplemented by regulatory decrees.
